值得閱讀的理由

  • 一次掌握 Nintendo Indie World 日美場次的多款獨立遊戲，快速了解各作品的玩法與特色。
  • 從解謎、卡牌策略到合作冒險與生活模擬，內容類型多元，方便讀者找到感興趣的作品。
  • 作者不只介紹遊戲內容，也點出適合的玩家族群，以及值得留意的合作、策略與探索元素。

摘要

解謎、卡牌與合作遊戲

作者介紹已推出的《Braid, Anniversary Edition》，這款由《Braid》與《The Witness》創作者帶來的解謎冒險遊戲，包含超過一千道手工設計謎題。玩家需要探索四個規則各異的世界，運用推箱子與特殊能力解開機關；隨著世界逐漸交疊，謎題也會融合不同機制，考驗玩家的思考與解題能力。

《One-Turn Kill》將牌組構築濃縮成一回合決勝：玩家以二十張卡牌組成牌組，設法在單次出手中擊倒敵人。《Super Chameleon》則是線上躲貓貓遊戲，躲藏者必須用顏色、圖案甚至姿勢融入場景；更新內容還加入新的團隊對戰規則、地圖與角色外觀。另一款輕鬆的清潔模擬遊戲讓玩家扮演可愛的大熊貓整理髒亂環境，並支援最多四人線上合作，搭配五十多首舒緩樂曲遊玩。

接著登場的是以「友情破壞」聞名的多人登山冒險：四名玩家扮演遭遇空難的探險者，必須在神祕山峰上互相協助、尋找離島方法。玩家要判斷落腳點、管理體力並善用道具，而混亂的物理效果與每日輪替地圖，可能讓隊友獲救，也可能讓人意外摔落。經典《都市傳說》也將登上 Switch，新增滑鼠風格操作與美術圖鑑，以復古畫風呈現都市怪談與詭異現象帶來的懸疑氣氛。

奇幻旅程與各式新玩法

《Sword of the Sea》是一款著重視覺與氛圍的冒險作品。神祕主角在古代遺跡甦醒後，將使用懸浮之劍高速穿越地形，尋找被掩埋的海洋、讓世界重獲生機；遊戲融合滑板、滑雪與衝浪般的移動感，並以美術與音樂營造奇幻景觀。另一款把任何事物都變成 Roguelike 的作品，則以推硬幣機為核心：玩家透過投幣達成各輪目標，取得額外硬幣、分數倍率或爆炸等效果，並搭配角色特性與道具打造連鎖反應，讓看似靠運氣的玩法也具有策略深度。

一款以日本桌遊平台為基礎的作品，支援最多四人共玩，收錄象棋、黑白棋、派對遊戲、TRPG 與推理遊戲等四十多種內容。它重視玩家互動與自由度，不會把所有規則都交由系統自動處理；不過日版伺服器目前似乎只有日文。接著介紹的悠閒生活遊戲以京都、青森、岐阜與別府為靈感，玩家要整理行李、規劃單車路線，替居民配送信件與包裹，並透過釣魚、打棒球、抓蟲、做壽司等活動認識小鎮居民，努力在夏季結束前重建神社、舉辦狸貓祭典。

《Spirit City》讓玩家來到連結人界與靈界的奇幻世界，探索、採集資源、協助迷途靈體，並與其他玩家交流或合作建造家園；隨著互動增加，遊戲還會逐步開放更多社交功能。《Goat Simulator》也將登上 Switch，玩家可以扮演山羊四處探索、完成任務或駕駛載具製造混亂，Switch 版改善了效能並收錄太空更新。節奏遊戲《Rhythm Doctor》則要求玩家配合病人的心跳進行手術，關卡會逐步加入錯拍、複雜拍號與複節奏等干擾，甚至用視覺效果誘使玩家按錯拍點；多元音樂與各關卡故事也增添了遊戲魅力。

生活模擬與更多值得關注的作品

《EvoCreo》融合生物進化與 Roguelike 元素，玩家透過進食累積經驗，選擇不同進化路線，讓每次遊玩都能嘗試新的組合。另一款受到生活模擬玩家期待的作品，乍看像《星露谷物語》，但舞台其實是魔法學院：主角來到海濱小鎮成為見習巫師，學習煉金術、占星與塔羅等知識，也能探索小鎮、結交居民、參加季節活動，或運用魔法經營小生意、協助居民。遊戲支援最多四人合作，既可獨自體驗學院生活，也能與朋友一同探索。

《Slime Rancher 2》延續前作的輕鬆魅力，玩家可在彩虹島探索古代科技與未知資源，收集各種史萊姆帶回牧場飼養，再用取得的材料升級設施、拓展探索範圍。最後，作者提到支援最多四人合作的浣熊模擬遊戲：玩家將和朋友扮演浣熊闖入人類領地，四處搗亂。影片在介紹這款作品時結束。

Hello, dear viewers, welcome back to my channel. I haven't even finished the last batch of new games, and now it's time for Nintendo's Indie World showcase . While there aren't any big first-party titles to headline, the platform is a great fit for indie games. Especially for players who enjoy handheld gaming, you can often find many hidden gems in these showcases. I've combined the content from both the Japanese and North American versions to walk you through them in the order of their release. Without further ado, let's get started. First up is the game already available on Switch, *Braid, Anniversary Edition* . It comes from the creators of*Braid* and*The Witness*, making it another puzzle-adventure that really tests your. brain. The most impressive part is that it includes over 1,000 hand-designed puzzles. Players must explore four distinct worlds with different rules, characters, and stories, using box-pushing and special abilities to solve various mechanical challenges. As the game progresses, these four unique worlds and characters begin to overlap, combining various puzzle mechanics and allowing you to develop new ways to approach gameplay you thought you'd already mastered—so don't underestimate it. The brilliance of this game lies in its puzzle design; for players who enjoy the sense of accomplishment that comes from figuring out solutions on their own , it holds a lot of appeal. Today's next. game has a title that explains its gameplay quite directly: *One-Turn Kill *. This title features retro pixel-art deck-building, but unlike standard card games, each battle lasts for only one turn. Players build a deck of 20 cards and must find a way to take the enemy out in one go. This essentially condenses the strategy and calculation of several turns in a traditional card game into a single burst of action, which should appeal to players who love studying deck builds and experimenting with combos. *Super Chameleon*is an online multiplayer hide-and-seek game where players are split into two teams. Here's the fun part: the hiders must.

manually paint themselves with various colors and patterns based on their surroundings to blend in just like a chameleon, even using poses to disguise themselves as objects in the scene. Whether you try to find a safe corner to hide in until the end or live dangerously by hiding in plain sight, it’s all up to your own creativity. This game was previously on Switch, and this update adds new team battle rules, maps , and character appearances. This could be considered a relaxing cleaning game— a casual simulation where you play as a cute giant panda, picking up cleaning tools to make messy environments neat and bright again. Moreover, you don't. just have to clean at your own pace; the game also supports up to four-player online co-op. You can enjoy the game's collection of over 50 slow-paced, relaxing tracks while cleaning alone, or invite friends to join in and see if you actually double your efficiency or just get in each other's way. This is the famous "break-up mountain climbing" game, a four-player co-op adventure where you play as a group of goofy-looking explorers who must reach the top of a mysterious peak after a plane crash to find a way off the island . The goal sounds simple, but the gameplay requires players to judge landing spots, manage stamina, and use. various items to help one another. Some maps rotate daily, and with the game's hilariously chaotic physics, when the moment of truth comes, whether you save your teammate or accidentally send them falling will really test your friendship . The classic "Urban Legend" game has now launched on Switch, adding new mouse-style controls, and an art gallery where you can view in-game scenes and previously unreleased character artwork . This is a suspense-adventure game centered on urban legends and bizarre phenomena. Beyond its eerie atmosphere, it features a highly distinctive art style that looks retro but excels in presentation and suspenseful vibes. "

Sword of the Sea" is a visually driven, atmospheric adventure game. You play as a mysterious protagonist who wakes up in an ancient ruin, using a hover-sword to zip across terrain at high speeds to find the buried ocean and restore life to the world. The game blends the feel of skating, snowboarding, and surfing, paired with a unique art style and music to explore its fantastic landscapes. Everything can be a roguelike—I wonder if any of you have played a coin-pusher machine before? The core goal of this game is to accumulate points by dropping coins to hit increasingly difficult targets in each round. As you push, you can acquire various special-effect coins. and items, such as extra coins, score multipliers, or even explosions that blast all the coins out of the machine at once. The game features different characters, each with their own unique coins and gameplay traits. You need to combine your coins and items strategically to trigger various effects . While it may look like it relies on luck, it actually offers plenty of depth for building and strategy, and it's incredibly satisfying to watch the coin explosions when chain reactions go off. This board game is based on a Japanese tabletop platform released for the Switch. One person can purchase it for up to four players to enjoy together, using the in-game chat to set up matches. . Beyond classics like chess and Othello , it includes various party games, TRPGs , and murder mystery titles, with over 40 games available at launch. What makes this title interesting is that it doesn't restrict all gameplay to rigid rules; instead, it offers significant freedom and emphasizes player interaction, as not every rule is automated by the system. However, the Japanese server version currently only appears to be in Japanese, though the visuals certainly capture that distinct summer vibe. The game is centered around four towns inspired by Kyoto, Aomori, Gifu, and Beppu, each with its own set of tasks waiting for you, the protagonist, to complete. Before setting off, the protagonist must pack parcels of different shapes, sizes, and weights.

into their backpack. You also have to plan your routes, figuring out how to use your bicycle to travel between these towns and deliver letters and packages to the residents, gradually getting to know everyone. You can also go fishing, play baseball, catch bugs, make sushi, or play the taiko drums. Use the money you earn and the materials you collect to rebuild the shrine before summer ends and host the annual Tanuki Festival. For players who enjoy life simulations and exploring small towns, or just want a relaxing game to enjoy while taking in the scenery, this is one to keep an eye on. Spirit City is also a life simulation game, but unlike typical single-player experiences, this title places a stronger emphasis on multiplayer online interaction. Players arrive in a fantastical land that. connects the human and spirit worlds, where they can explore, gather resources , and help lost spirits while interacting with other players. Meet others and work together to build your home. You can choose to avoid meeting others, or you can make friends and participate in various activities. As interactions between players increase, the game will gradually unlock more social features. Goat Simulator has arrived on the Switch, and it’s a hilarious game that kills physics engines. The characters can cause all sorts of unexpected comedic moments with whatever they do. You can explore all kinds of missions or just drive various vehicles around wildly. The Switch version features improved performance and also includes the space update. Rhythm Doctor is somewhat similar to. Rhythm Heaven, yet quite different, though both share the concept of simplified controls paired with imaginative level design. What sets this game apart is that you play as an intern , performing surgeries by matching the patient's heartbeat. The game features various tracks, and as you progress, it introduces distractions like off-beat rhythms, complex time signatures, and polyrhythms. The visuals are also designed to trick you into pressing buttons at the wrong time, so even if you've mastered the music, it's easy to slip up. Each level has its own story, which, combined with diverse musical styles and creative level mechanics, makes it quite engaging. "EvoCreo"( Everything can evolve) blends biological evolution with roguelike mechanics. You constantly consume food to gain experience and choose different.

evolutionary paths, allowing you to try unique combinations in every run. This game is one that many fans of life simulation games have been waiting for quite a while. At first glance, this title looks a bit like Stardew Valley, but instead of farming, you're off to a magic academy. You play as a protagonist who arrives in a seaside town to begin their studies as an apprentice wizard. You'll learn everything from the basics of alchemy, astrology, and tarot to various magical rituals. In your spare time, you can explore the town, make friends with the locals, participate in seasonal events, or even use your magic to run a small business and help townsfolk solve their problems. This game supports up to four-player co-op, so you can experience magical school. life at your own pace or explore the town together with friends. Slime Rancher 2 continues the charm of its predecessor. Rainbow Island is not only home to colorful, quirky slimes, but it also hides ancient technology, unknown resources, and plenty of secrets waiting to be discovered. Players can freely roam the island, collect different types of slimes to raise on their ranch, and use harvested resources to upgrade and expand, gradually widening their exploration. The game’s relaxed and vibrant atmosphere makes it a very chill experience. Raccoon Simulator, or rather "Troublemaker Simulator," supports up to four-player co-op. You and your friends play as raccoons, causing chaos in human. territory. You can raid trash cans, steal food, snatch all sorts of random items, or even break into houses to mess with anything your little paws can grab . Along the way, you'll have to complete all sorts of absurd missions. Once you cause enough of a stir, people will come to catch you, and balancing destruction with escaping capture is a big part of the fun. The visuals are super retro, using a Game Boy Color aesthetic combined with open-world exploration and RPG gameplay. The protagonist and their partner travel along the coast, exploring the city and meeting all sorts of interesting characters. You'll also get sidetracked by side quests and get to experience various mini-games. This game is currently available as a demo. If you like retro pixel art and want to.

play a relaxing RPG with exploration and story elements, you should give this a try. As for this game, the name is quite absurd, and the gameplay is even more so . Players take on the role of someone with an arm that can stretch at will, even slithering around like a snake. Each level features different environments and goals, requiring you to think outside the box and utilize this magical arm to complete tasks. It’s clearly a wild and hilariously wacky title. Wait, here comes another absurd one. As the name suggests, in this game , it's not just about getting your ball into the hole, but most importantly, keeping others from doing the same. The game allows up to eight players on the course at once. It’s not your typical turn-based golf; everyone just rushes. the course together. You can calculate angles and power to sink your shot quickly, or use various items—or should I say, weapons—to fight, or even drive a golf cart to knock people away. Various course hazards, and even traps like landmines, will keep things challenging . The action-adventure game Jade Wind feels a bit like Zelda. Players take on the role of a protagonist stepping onto a continent full of the unknown to restore the balance of an ancient civilization. The game's world features various regions, including mountain spirit lands, hidden caves, and ancient ruins. The protagonist can use a grappling hook and special movements to quickly traverse terrain. You will. challenge beasts influenced by chaotic forces and meet companions to explore and fight alongside. This title is created by a group of developers. It features platforming and puzzle-solving , with a striking visual style composed of distinct colors. The game is set in a city filled with spirit beasts and dangerous robots. Players will adventure through five unique areas, each with distinct environments, gameplay styles, and designs. Beyond platforming and puzzles, it also incorporates fast-paced combat. Double-dog formation—in this game, two players control puppies on a cooperative adventure through a haunted house. You can customize your dog's breed, color, and accessories, with.

mechanics designed around canine abilities, like sniffing out clues, digging up hidden items, or barking in emergencies. The haunted house is full of strange rooms that require players to cooperate, find clues to solve puzzles, and face monsters together. Journey of the Frog and Fox is inspired by folklore , a game with a strong Japanese supernatural atmosphere. Players take on the role of a fox girl exploring a mysterious island with her frog companion. The game's environmental design is quite unique, featuring Japanese-style streets with torii gates , alongside neon signs and various buildings full of nostalgia; the lighting makes the world look both dreamlike and slightly eerie. In terms. of gameplay, players need to explore the island while lighting up shrines scattered throughout to illuminate the surroundings, uncovering new paths and hidden content, all while being wary of monsters lurking in the shadows. Insurmountable is quite a hardcore climbing simulator that also functions as a survival game with a strong sense of immersion; you need to properly use various climbing gear, observe rock faces, find footholds, judge where to place your hands and feet to carve out your own route, and manage supplies by finding suitable spots to rest and replenish. Every stretch of rock is like a puzzle to be solved; the game offers selectable difficulties, so you can. either try the challenges of high-difficulty climbing or experience this journey at your own pace. In Lost and Found Co., players are guided by a goddess to help townspeople locate lost items; the game’s scenes are filled with interactive elements, many of which trigger fun reactions, and you can even play with up to four people to see who has the sharpest eye. As each request unfolds, players not only need to use their imagination to search the screen, but they will also gradually get to know the residents and learn the stories behind every object. Inspired by classic titles like Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy, this game's theme revolves around traveling through time. Players will assemble a team of heroes from.

different eras, adventuring from the ancient past to the distant future, ultimately unraveling the secrets that threaten the boundaries of the timeline . The combat segment adopts traditional turn-based RPG gameplay with some modern design twists; players can use time-manipulation abilities to break enemy defenses and coordinate with teammates to launch powerful combo attacks. As teammates from different eras continue to join, coordinating character skill combinations becomes a crucial part of your build. One of the lead creators of Windblown is a designer of Dead Cells; this title combines action combat with fast-paced, fluid, and skill-based melee fighting, while the visuals and setting have an old-school arcade feel. The protagonist rises up against a massive criminal. organization controlling the city; you can decide the order in which to take them down, and those left for later will become stronger, but as you defeat each organization, the city will regain its vitality, unlocking more facilities, shortcuts, weapons, and combat skills to ensure each run accumulates new growth. Terrifying co-op and physics-based chaos combine to ensure everything goes wrong all at once. In this game, players take on the role of robots tasked with moving objects out, but the area is crawling with horrific monsters; carrying items is hard enough, and you’ll have to constantly watch out for sudden dangers . However, more often than not, it’s not the monsters that make you nervous, but. your unreliable teammates. This one blends sci-fi settings, campus life, and an intense, modified version of dodgeball. The protagonist must defeat the eight elite students at the top of the academy within 10 days, with battles centered around a sport called " Dodgeball." Players need to use ball attacks and various movement techniques to take on opponents, each with their own unique abilities and combat styles. Every battle feels more like a major boss fight, requiring you to observe the opponent’s moves, find openings, and break through their defense. Outside of combat, the protagonist will make new friends at the academy and gradually uncover the secrets behind the school. That's the lineup, ranging from relaxing , healing life sims and puzzle games to.

hardcore titles. There's parkour action-adventure, along with plenty of multiplayer games perfect for playing with friends—there's basically something for everyone. Some of these indie titles have already gained popularity on PC, giving fans of handheld gaming new options, so feel free to chat about them in the comments section. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解《龍族教義 2》在 Switch 上的畫面取捨、DLSS 技術應用及補幀模式帶來的延遲影響。
  • 掌握大型擴充內容所帶來的北方新地圖、試煉迷宮與隨機詞條裝備等全新遊戲要素。
  • 全方位評估遊戲反便利的硬派探索機制與卡普空頂級打擊感，判斷是否符合自身遊玩偏好。

摘要

移植效能與畫面幀率實測

作者指出《龍族教義 2》登陸 Switch 平台的表現備受關注，實體版需額外下載約 49GB 空間。在畫面表現上，該版本雖然縮減了全域光照與部分地表貼圖細節，但藉由 DLSS 重建技術讓整體畫面保持清晰銳利。在運行幀率方面，未開啟補幀時浮動在 35 至 50 幀之間，鎖定 30 幀時則因影格生成步調不穩而略顯卡頓；然而一旦開啟補幀模式，絕大多數場景均能維持在 60 幀的流暢度。儘管該模式會引入約 130 毫秒的操作延遲，但考慮到本作著重招式前後搖與重量感的硬派戰鬥設計，作者認為補幀帶來的視覺流暢度依舊帶來了超出預期的遊戲體驗。

擴充內容與反便利的冒險機制

隨著大型擴充內容推出，遊戲追加了風格截然不同的北方地圖與 12 座試煉迷宮，玩家在遊戲初期即可前往挑戰，透過探索獲得神秘物品並鑑定出帶有隨機數值的強力裝備，有效彌補了本篇怪物種類不足的遺憾。作者提醒玩家，本作的敘事手法較為零碎且任務導引極度薄弱，沒有便捷的隨意傳送與坐騎系統，背包負重與漫長的跑圖過程完全不迎合現代玩家的便利習慣，甚至十分考驗玩家的耐心。

硬派沉浸感與卡普空極致戰鬥

作者強調，這款遊戲的魅力在於高度仿真的冒險沉浸感。白天與黑夜的視野差距與怪物生態營造出未知恐懼，野外紮營烹飪、牛車遭受奇襲，以及追隨者系統與路過 NPC 共同參與的混亂團戰，都讓奇幻世界顯得無比真實。最核心的吸引力依然來自卡普空頂尖的動作戰鬥系統，拳拳到肉的近戰手感搭配魄力十足的強大魔法，為願意沉浸其中的玩家提供了無可替代的冒險樂趣。

Hello dear viewers, welcome back to my channel. Capcom's uniquely styled action game Dragon's Dogma 2, just like its predecessor, recently received the massive expansion "Dark Arisen," and it has just launched on the Switch in its complete form. This series is quite unique; its flaws are just as prominent as its strengths. On one hand, coming from the "action masters" at Capcom, Dragon's Dogma still boasts the best combat feel in the genre to this day. The stylish, hardcore melee combat combined with explosive magic in a fantasy setting creates an incredible atmosphere, and the pawn system is also quite distinctive. But at the same time , its drawbacks are very obvious, especially in open-world exploration. and quest design, which feel like they were intentionally made to spite the convenience of modern gaming. There is a massive amount of running around, fast travel was heavily restricted in early versions, and without a guide, quest markers are very weak, forcing you to figure things out yourself. Add in inventory weight and enemies that constantly interrupt your travel rhythm , and it really feels like a true adventure. However, whether this adventure feels fulfilling or just tests your patience depends entirely on whether it clicks with your personal taste. There was another point of high interest when this Switch version was announced: the 2024 launch of Dragon's Dogma 2 had a disastrous performance in terms of optimization. At the time, it released right around the same time as Rise of the Ronin, leading to a joke.

that both games sent players back to the past: one had visuals that couldn't keep up with the times, and the other had a frame rate that couldn't keep up; the former fixed optimization through updates, while the latter relied on hardware patches. In reality, Dragon's Dogma 2's issues went beyond just low frame rates, as the game almost always features group combat—besides the player, nearby NPCs often join in, making the battle effects dense and intense. I played the original PS5 version, and once combat started in the mid-to-late game, the frame rate would plummet like a rollercoaster, only becoming comfortable later on the PS5 Pro. So, how does this Switch version perform? The physical version of Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen comes on a game card, but it requires about 49GB of additional storage space. According. to professional performance reviews, this version mainly removes global illumination, reduces some ground texture details, lowers reflection precision and some light source effects , and NPCs in the environment often only load once you are within a certain distance. However, its shadow performance is better than the SS version, and thanks to what appears to be DLSS reconstruction, this version is clearer and sharper with richer texture details. There is also a lot of running around in the gameplay, and the delay in loading environmental elements is kept within an acceptable range. All footage in this video is actual gameplay, which you can use as a reference. Regarding the frame rate performance, it is a mixed bag; Capcom has provided an option for frame generation while locked at 30 fps in this version. When frame rate locking.

and frame generation are turned off, the game stays mostly between 35 and 50 fps. However, due to frequent frame rate fluctuations, it doesn't perform well, and even the 30 fps lock feels stuttery because of the unstable frame generation pacing. Turning on the frame generation mode is a game changer. In my tests, whether running through the map or in combat with heavy effects, it stays at 60 fps most of the time. Even when quickly turning the camera while moving, it rarely drops, only dipping to around 40 fps during some intense effect-heavy moments. It quickly returns to 60, but enabling frame generation does introduce a certain amount of input latency. According to. simulation tests, it adds about 130 milliseconds, which makes character controls feel somewhat heavy. In terms of actual experience, the input lag is noticeable, especially when adjusting the camera and chaining skills quickly during combat, which can feel a bit sluggish. However, Dragon's Dogma's combat design is quite hardcore and emphasizes a sense of weight. Since all attacks have distinct wind-up and recovery animations, this latency isn't as impactful during general exploration and most combat as it would be in games that prioritize fast-paced, fluid movement. Personally, I played from start to finish with frame generation turned on, as I value smoothness more in this type of game. But those sensitive to input response should be.

aware: frame generation looks smooth, but it feels subtly delayed, and turning it off or not locking to 30 fps results in a lack of visual fluidity. The game's experience should be viewed as a whole; considering the original optimization of Dragon's Dogma, the experience in the current version's frame generation mode is better than expected. The main thing I suggest is that Capcom needs to fix the frame pacing issues in the locked 30fps mode, improve VRR performance in the unlocked framerate mode, and reduce input lag in the 30fps mode. If they can improve at least one of these three, the experience will certainly be much better. More importantly, the base game has received successive updates, making the content and playability of this expansion much richer and more polished. than in the early versions. Looking at the "Awakener," it's only been out for a few days. Currently, its Metacritic average is 84, and the user score is 8.2, so the majority of players are satisfied. Next, let's talk specifically about the game itself. Dragon's Dogma 2 has undergone major updates, including a large number of adjustments to system details. As a follow-up expansion, the "Dark Arisen" content adds even more, including a new northern map with completely different terrain and characteristics from the base game, and 12 trial labyrinths where you can obtain rare equipment and special items. You can visit this new map early in the base game's progression. In theory, the enemies here are tuned to late-game difficulty with very high stats, but since you can get mysterious items by farming mobs or exploring, and then have them appraised.

to unlock powerful weapons and gear with random stats, you can actually farm them in the mid-to-early game by scavenging or using methods like having your pawns shield each other. There are quite a few new enemies as well. Honestly, there are still a lot of " palette swaps," but it at least makes up for the regret of the base game having too few monster types, which felt like a waste of such a good combat system. For those who haven't played the original Dragon's Dogma 2, this is essentially a more polished, content-rich, and complete enhanced version. The plot of Dragon's Dogma has a strong blend of Japanese style and Western fantasy. Players start off as an amnesiac. As the "Arisen" who lost their heart, you set off on an adventure involving the throne, a dragon, and the secrets behind this. world. I want to manage your expectations here: if you're looking for an RPG with rich narrative performances, nuanced character development, and tons of spectacular cutscenes, Dragon's Dogma 2 might not meet your expectations. Its narrative style is quite disjointed, and some character portrayals and plot progressions are relatively brief. You might even be confused when you receive certain quests, and somehow they just push forward to the next stage inexplicably. On top of that, the quest guidance isn't always very clear; if you don't use a guide, you'll often feel like whether a quest goes smoothly or not is just a matter of luck. From another perspective, this design is tied to the game's overall philosophy. Dragon's Dogma 2 feels a lot like those.

classic Western RPGs that turn a fantasy world into a stage you can truly participate in. There are so many systemic details, which help deepen the immersion of your adventure. It doesn't always put all the information right in front of you; instead, it lets players gradually uncover the details of the world as they explore. You aren't just following quest markers from start to finish; you have to consider how to get somewhere, whether you have enough supplies, and the fact that it gets dark while you're out in the wild. Visibility drops as night falls. During the day, you can spot enemies from afar and choose whether to engage, but at night, dangers lurk everywhere, including monsters that don't appear in the daylight. This is especially true when entering a new area; that sense of the unknown, not knowing what might suddenly pop out, is palpable. Plus,. you have teammates, and you might occasionally run into other NPCs—some might jump in to help when you're in a pinch, leading to a chaotic free-for-all. What was once quiet suddenly becomes lively, and then you see a campfire in the distance and hurry over to rest. The cooking animations in the game always make me hungry. Even when you're traveling by oxcart, you might be ambushed, and you have to be careful not to wreck the cart while fighting. This specific, granular, and immersive sense of adventure is a unique part of the experience—if it happens to suit your taste. But the prerequisite for getting into it is accepting that it doesn't cater to modern player habits. The quest guidance really tests your patience; side quests, in particular, are easy to miss without a guide. There.

are no mounts, so traversing the map takes up a significant amount of playtime. The art style is also quite understated, so players who enjoy sightseeing while exploring fantasy worlds or who hope to see all sorts of exotic wonders in different regions might not be satisfied. Yet, at the same time, Dragon's Dogma 2 has an aspect that is most intuitively attractive: the combat. Capcom's experience with action games is clearly on display here. Even in the first game , casting a spell felt like you could physically feel the impact. The modern version offers three difficulty levels right from the start. After all, for those less skilled at action games, you can still have a great time by leveling up and upgrading gear, while hardcore players can jump straight into high-difficulty combat. As a follow-up expansion, the "Dark Arisen" content adds even more, including a new northern map with completely different terrain and characteristics from the base game, and 12 trial labyrinths where you can obtain rare equipment and special items. You can visit this new map early in the base game's progression. In theory, the enemies here are tuned to late-game difficulty with very high stats, but since you can get mysterious items by farming mobs or exploring, and then have them appraised.

to unlock powerful weapons and gear with random stats, you can actually farm them in the mid-to-early game by scavenging or using methods like having your pawns shield each other. There are quite a few new enemies as well. Honestly, there are still a lot of " palette swaps," but it at least makes up for the regret of the base game having too few monster types, which felt like a waste of such a good combat system. For those who haven't played the original Dragon's Dogma 2, this is essentially a more polished, content-rich, and complete enhanced version. The plot of Dragon's Dogma has a strong blend of Japanese style and Western fantasy. Players start off as an amnesiac. As the "Arisen" who lost their heart, you set off on an adventure involving the throne, a dragon, and the secrets behind this. world. I want to manage your expectations here: if you're looking for an RPG with rich narrative performances, nuanced character development, and tons of spectacular cutscenes, Dragon's Dogma 2 might not meet your expectations. Its narrative style is quite disjointed, and some character portrayals and plot progressions are relatively brief. You might even be confused when you receive certain quests, and somehow they just push forward to the next stage inexplicably. On top of that, the quest guidance isn't always very clear; if you don't use a guide, you'll often feel like whether a quest goes smoothly or not is just a matter of luck. From another perspective, this design is tied to the game's overall philosophy. Dragon's Dogma 2 feels a lot like those.

classic Western RPGs that turn a fantasy world into a stage you can truly participate in. There are so many systemic details, which help deepen the immersion of your adventure. It doesn't always put all the information right in front of you; instead, it lets players gradually uncover the details of the world as they explore. You aren't just following quest markers from start to finish; you have to consider how to get somewhere, whether you have enough supplies, and the fact that it gets dark while you're out in the wild. Visibility drops as night falls. During the day, you can spot enemies from afar and choose whether to engage, but at night, dangers lurk everywhere, including monsters that don't appear in the daylight. This is especially true when entering a new area; that sense of the unknown, not knowing what might suddenly pop out, is palpable. Plus,. you have teammates, and you might occasionally run into other NPCs—some might jump in to help when you're in a pinch, leading to a chaotic free-for-all. What was once quiet suddenly becomes lively, and then you see a campfire in the distance and hurry over to rest. The cooking animations in the game always make me hungry. Even when you're traveling by oxcart, you might be ambushed, and you have to be careful not to wreck the cart while fighting. This specific, granular, and immersive sense of adventure is a unique part of the experience—if it happens to suit your taste. But the prerequisite for getting into it is accepting that it doesn't cater to modern player habits. The quest guidance really tests your patience; side quests, in particular, are easy to miss without a guide. There.

are no mounts, so traversing the map takes up a significant amount of playtime. The art style is also quite understated, so players who enjoy sightseeing while exploring fantasy worlds or who hope to see all sorts of exotic wonders in different regions might not be satisfied. Yet, at the same time, Dragon's Dogma 2 has an aspect that is most intuitively attractive: the combat. Capcom's experience with action games is clearly on display here. Even in the first game , casting a spell felt like you could physically feel the impact. The modern version offers three difficulty levels right from the start. After all, for those less skilled at action games, you can still have a great time by leveling up and upgrading gear, while hardcore players can jump straight into high-difficulty combat. In the thick of it, beyond basic attacks and various. class-specific skills, you have many ways to handle different enemies, including utilizing environmental objects. You can grab smaller enemies directly to break their guard and throw them, or perform an execution after they become unbalanced; for large enemies, you can also cause them to stumble or climb onto them to deal massive damage to their weak points. As an action game developed by Capcom, Dragon's Dogma combat has a very interesting aspect: its action design balances technical depth with visceral satisfaction, and the combat philosophy for each vocation is distinctly different. Take the Fighter, a melee vocation, for example; you can feel a clear sense of weight in its attacks, and the focus is quite unique—the Fighter's balance of offense and defense emphasizes anticipation, and the feeling of landing a well-timed strike is both solid and satisfying.

The Sorcerer offers a completely different experience; the most powerful spells require longer incantation times , but once successfully cast and landed , the visual effects and area-of-effect damage are truly staggering. What's more, you can change vocations as often as you like. In the early game, you can get comfortable with the four basic vocations—Fighter, Archer, Thief, and Mage—and later, by progressing or completing specific quests, you'll unlock classes like Warrior, Sorcerer, Magick Archer, Mystic Spearhand, Trickster, and Warfarer. Each vocation also has corresponding Maister skills, and the Arisen can further gain vocation bonuses and skill enhancements through special items. As you continue to fight and level up your vocations, both the protagonist and the main pawn can unlock vocation abilities, which. can then be equipped even after changing classes. By trying other vocations as you progress through the game, you'll discover that when facing the same powerful enemy, switching classes can completely transform your entire combat experience. At the same time, the Dragon's Dogma series features another iconic system: Pawns, which are an incredibly important part of this entire adventurous journey. They aren't just there to help with damage output or tanking hits; at the very beginning, you will create your own main Pawn, who will level up alongside you, and Pawns can even learn specialized skills throughout your journey. Players will constantly recruit other players 'or official Pawns at Riftstones or along the road based on party needs to form a team of four to explore the world and challenge monsters; likewise, your own main Pawn.

can be hired by other players. The interesting thing about this system is, first of all, Pawns have various inclinations; beyond just their speech habits, these affect their tendencies in exploration and combat. For instance , a Kindhearted pawn might prioritize suppressing enemies and providing enchantments, while a Calm one might focus on defense and evasion. Additionally, Pawns retain memories of their adventures; if they have previously experienced certain quests, map locations, or combat scenarios, they will offer you hints and guidance. You can check the quest menu and badges to see if your pawn has knowledge of a specific quest, monster combat, or area exploration. Of course, AI pawns aren't as reliable as human teammates; sometimes they’re quite clever, syncing their attacks and support perfectly with yours, but other times. they can be hit-or-miss when you need directions or guidance. Regardless, Dragon’s Dogma’s pawn system offers the flexibility of a single-player game , letting you start your journey anytime with a diverse team of various appearances and vocations who chat while traveling and proactively help out during combat. And since pawns come from different players, you'll often discover some really interesting characters, making this an unconventional action RPG with very distinct strengths and weaknesses. If you prioritize action combat, enjoy experimenting with different vocation playstyles, want to challenge massive monsters, and don't mind a bit of exploration overhead, then Dragon's.

Dogma 2 is worth a try. From the first game to now, the series has always had design choices that invite criticism, but its sense of adventure is unique, and its combat experience is truly irreplaceable; the satisfying weight of hits, action design, and the spectacle of magic filling the screen are what keep its loyal fanbase hooked. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解《朧村正》如何以和風怪談、美麗手繪畫面與容易上手的戰鬥，留下鮮明特色。
  • 掌握新版整合六段故事、調整秘奧義系統與改善移動節奏等重要變化。
  • 看見作者對戰鬥自訂深度與技能平衡的期待，也了解老玩家與新玩家各自值得關注的內容。

摘要

經典作品迎來新版本

作者介紹，Vanillaware以精緻的手繪美術與翻新傳統玩法聞名，作品數量不多，卻常憑獨特風格讓玩家印象深刻。《朧村正》原於2009年推出，2013年推出PS Vita版，如今將推出強化版，登上Switch、PS4、PS5與PC，並收錄四篇「元祿怪奇譚」DLC故事。作者參加了由Bilibili舉辦的試玩活動，將結合實際體驗與官方資訊，分享新版特色。

手繪怪談風格與爽快戰鬥

故事以日本元祿時代為背景，城鎮、森林、人物、妖怪與頭目皆呈現濃厚的時代氛圍。角色設計帶有傳統繪卷般的細膩感，又融入幽異氣息；Vanillaware招牌的精美料理也依然登場。戰鬥則以普通攻擊、跳躍、衝刺、收刀機制與秘奧義組成，操作直覺，玩家即使不熟悉複雜指令，也能打出流暢連段；同時還得把握時機防禦、彈開攻擊或將飛行道具反擊回去。

新版收錄完整故事並調整秘奧義

作者認為，舊版雖然美術出色、容易上手，但後期戰鬥可能變得重複，章節間往返也會拖慢節奏，長時間對付精英敵人與頭目時尤其容易感到單調。新版一開始便能選擇主角鬼助與百姬，以及四位DLC主角的六段故事，內容與角色戰鬥風格都更完整。

更重要的改動在於秘奧義系統。舊版的技能綁定特定妖刀，玩家若想使用某招，就必須裝備對應武器；到了後期，也容易只依賴少數能力與數值較強的刀。新版讓鬼助與百姬能使用太刀及大太刀，逐步學會各種秘技後，再自由配置到地面與空中各三個欄位。玩家可依照習慣組合招式，並強化常用秘技，讓戰鬥技能不再受限於手持的刀。

武器養成、探索與戰鬥節奏

妖刀本身仍然重要，其攻防數值、個別特性與戰鬥中切換武器的時機，都會影響作戰方式。鬼助與百姬可以鍛造新刀，並使用素材強化；遊戲共有108種秘技，搭配多樣武器，鼓勵玩家嘗試不同組合。其他主角則保有各自的成長方式，例如透過修行學習技能，或為武器添加特殊效果，因此六段故事雖然整合在同一版本，角色特色並未被統一成單一養成系統。

新版也提供多種快速移動方式，玩家甚至能直接前往尚未探索的區域，不過角色實力不足時可能會遭遇苦戰。沿海地區可以搭船出海、釣魚，也可能遭到海防勢力襲擊。移動更便利，能減少往返花費的時間；作者在試玩中也注意到，部分戰鬥的敵人數量似乎增加，並會連續出現多波敵人，讓玩家有更多機會運用新技能組合。

收藏內容與發售前的觀察

試玩活動工作人員透露，新版會在原有內容中加入更多溫泉場景與全新料理。遊戲還設有美術收藏館，收錄插畫、分鏡、場景與劇本；此外也能遊玩原版內容及《朧村正》的DLC，以高畫質重溫舊作。對喜歡橫向動作遊戲、日本民俗傳說或Vanillaware美術風格的玩家而言，這款作品值得留意；老玩家則可特別關注秘奧義系統的改變。

作者認為，108種秘技與妖刀特性結合後，理應讓玩家依照敵人與頭目選擇不同打法，從積極進攻到追求高難度連段都能找到發揮空間。不過，若最後玩家仍只挑出最強的幾招一路使用，豐富的自訂選項就可能淪為少數固定解法。因此，正式版的戰鬥平衡將是關鍵：各種技能是否都有實用價值，能否促使玩家因應不同敵人改變戰術，仍須等到發售後才能確認。

================================================

Hello, dear viewers, and welcome back to my channel. Vanillaware is known for its signature beautiful hand-drawn art style and for adding fresh elements to various traditional gameplay mechanics. The studio's output may not be high, but most of their games leave a deep impression on players who enjoy their style, as it is so distinct. Because their games were long restricted to specific platforms, many have hoped these classics would be ported to all systems, and it would be even better if they received modern enhancements. Back in the last generation, I felt*Dragon's Crown*was a perfect fit for other platforms, but sadly we never saw it happen; however, Vanillaware's early classic action RPG, *Muramasa*, is finally getting a new version. Beyond improving the resolution, adding new.

system elements, and refining the combat experience, it also integrates the four previously released DLC stories, "Genroku Legends." This enhanced "Muramasa: The Demon Blade" complete edition will arrive on Switch, PS4, PS5, and PC on February 4th next year. I recently participated in a demo event for this title hosted by Bilibili , which gave me a glimpse into what it has to offer. Today, I'll combine my hands-on impressions with officially released information to discuss how this classic title performs now. The original*Muramasa*was first released in 2009, followed by a PS Vita version in 2013. Speaking of Vanillaware's highly sophisticated hand-drawn art, the style actually differs depending on the background of each specific game. * Muramasa*is set during Japan’s.

Genroku era; everything from the towns and forests to the various characters, yokai, and bosses is a core element of the game. The character designs carry a style reminiscent of traditional picture scrolls—to put it simply, they are both exquisite and infused with an eerie, supernatural vibe. Under this unique "kaidan"(ghost story) theme , the characters and the scenery you encounter on your adventure are very visually appealing, not to mention Vanillaware's other signature element: the food, which definitely won't be missing. Beyond the visuals, *Muramasa* has another very distinctive feature: a combat system that is simple, intuitive , and easy to pick up, yet allows for a wide variety of flashy, satisfying combos. With normal attacks, jumping, and dashing, combined with the game's blade-sheathing mechanics and secret.

arts, you can easily pull off fluid combos even if you're just mashing buttons. Furthermore, centered around this blade system, there is a strong connection between offense and defense; while dishing out combos, you also need to watch for enemy attacks to parry or deflect projectiles back at them. The benefit of this design is that you don't need complex inputs to quickly find your rhythm in the progressive combat. That’s why my impression of Muramasa back then was that it had outstanding art, was easy to pick up, and was a highly satisfying side-scrolling action game. The problem is that in 2026, player tastes have long since changed. Combat in the original version could easily become repetitive later on, there was some back-and-forth backtracking between.

chapters, the pacing of certain encounters wasn't tight enough, and combat could feel monotonous when facing elite enemies and bosses for long periods. There are still many players who love the art style and stories from back then, but since a new version is coming out, wouldn't it be a wasted opportunity if they didn't make some adjustments? So, what exactly has been changed in this new version? First , looking at the content: the original game focused on two protagonists, Kisuke and Momohime, whose adventures revolved around demon blades, each with their own emphasis. This formed the main content, while the subsequent Genroku Legends DLC added four more protagonists, each with independent backstories and distinct combat styles. This new version includes all of that content, and all six stories are.

available to choose from the very beginning. In terms of playable characters and story depth for this genre, there’s no need to worry about the amount of content here. While the visual improvements and content integration are the most immediately noticeable things, I personally feel that the adjustments to the combat system are more important, because the original Muramasa had a very unique combat logic. In this game, the demon blades aren't just weapons; they combine character progression with combat skills. Each blade has its own attack and defense stats, and is tied to a specific secret art. Players can carry three blades at once and switch between them at any time during combat, utilizing different blade traits to handle strong enemies. Furthermore, a blade's spirit power is linked to both defense and the release of special.

secret arts. You can use simple basic attacks to chain combos, and seize the right timing during chaotic battles to defend or parry. While this logic is theoretically uncomplicated and allows for some variety—making for smooth, high-combo combat—there is a problem: since each skill is tied to a specific blade, if you find a skill particularly useful or if a fight requires a specific solution, you are forced to equip that weapon. By the late game, as you collect more blades, it becomes easy to stick to just a few "strongest" ones based on stats and skills, leaving the rest to gather dust. For this demo, the developers specifically emphasized the adjustments to the secret art.

system. In this game, Oboro and Momohime can use two types of weapons: the katana and the nodachi. As you continue to fight, you can gradually learn the secret techniques of each weapon and then freely assign them to three ground and three aerial slots. In this way, besides the skills inherent to the weapon currently equipped, players can freely combine different attack styles based on their own combat habits. Previously, if you wanted a specific skill, you had to switch to the corresponding demon blade, but now you can configure your skills in advance, allowing for more flexible combos during battle. You can even further strengthen the secret techniques that you find particularly useful. While skills are a major focus, the demon blades themselves remain highly significant; their stats, individual traits, and switching during.

combat are still crucial. Oboro and Momohime can use the forging function to create various new blades, and these weapons can also be further strengthened using materials. In short, skills are no longer limited to specific weapons. With a total of 108 secret techniques paired with a vast array of weapons, players have more incentive to try different combinations . Other protagonists have their own ways to grow, such as using the training function to learn skills or add special effects to their weapons. So, although the six stories have been integrated, the game doesn't simply force all characters to share one growth system; instead, it preserves their unique combat styles as much as possible. The game also features various quick-travel methods, even allowing you to run directly to areas you haven't explored yet, though you'll likely struggle if your character isn't.

strong enough. In coastal areas, you can take a boat out to sea; not only can you catch fish, but you might also be attacked by coastal defense groups. Traveling between chapters and areas is much more convenient, so players focused on combat don't have to spend too much time getting around, allowing for a faster pace when fighting monsters, exploring, or progressing through the story. Additionally, the number of enemies in encounters during my playthrough seems higher than in the original version. In the original, some early-game battles would end just as you found your rhythm with a combo, but in this version, some encounters feature multiple continuous waves of enemies, likely to complement the revamped skill system. Since combat now offers more offensive options, increasing the enemy count and battle frequency is only logical to ensure.

these skill combinations actually get put to use, right? Also, for those who love Vanillaware's style, the staff at the demo mentioned that this version will add more hot spring scenes and brand-new food items to the original content. If you've played the original, this Muramasa: The Demon Blade remake features an art gallery with illustrations, storyboards, scenes, and scripts. It also includes the original game and the Oboro Muramasa DLC, allowing you to re-experience the original adventure in high definition. For those who haven't heard of Muramasa before, if you enjoy side-scrolling action games and are interested in Japanese folklore themes and Vanillaware's art style, this remake is definitely worth keeping an eye on. As for veteran players, besides the sense of nostalgia, I think it's worth paying.

attention to the adjustments made to the Secret Art system. In theory, after learning this vast array of skills and combining them with the blade's own attributes and traits, different players might choose unique skill combinations when facing groups of enemies or tough bosses. For instance, some might prefer aggressive playstyles , while others might pursue high-difficulty combos and pursuit attacks. However, it could also end up being a case of just picking the strongest few out of the 108 Secret Arts and using them exclusively throughout the game. Therefore, combat balance in the official release will be crucial. If certain combinations are clearly better than others, then the seemingly vast room for customization could end up boiling down to a few fixed "optimal" solutions. The key is how to ensure most skills have their.

own viable purpose, giving players the incentive to try different tactics when facing different types of enemies. We'll have to wait for the final release to see how it turns out. Specifically, whether the Secret Art system can truly change the approach to combat is something we'll have to wait and see. Alright, that's all for today's video. Thanks for watching, and if you liked...
